rules.title: Heat and air-quality alerts overlap
rules.threshold: Two distinct, locally applicable heat and Air Quality Alert messages with overlapping validity windows.
rules.mechanism: Plans to reduce heat exposure also need to account for outdoor air quality. An air-quality alert can concern pollutants other than smoke.
rules.action: Read both official instructions and plan for cooling and cleaner air together. Check which pollutant the air-quality alert identifies.
rules.coverage_note: Checked currently issued alerts for this place; future alerts can still be issued.

rules.title: Recent unhealthy particle reading during a heat alert
rules.threshold: An active local heat alert and the closest recent measured PM2.5 monitor within 50 km reporting AQI above 100. Reading must be no older than 3 hours and fall within the heat-alert window.
rules.mechanism: The nearby monitor reports particle pollution while a heat alert applies here. It does not establish pollution at this exact place or predict future exposure.
rules.action: Check current local air quality and identify a cool location with cleaner air. Do not make an indoor space dangerously hot in an attempt to keep smoke out.
guidance: EPA: cooling and cleaner indoor air
rules.coverage_note: 0 active heat alert(s) with known times. Closest recent monitor 5.0 km away reports AQI 34; only its observation time is assessed, with no projection into future hours.

rules.title: Winter and wind alerts overlap
rules.threshold: Two distinct, locally applicable winter-weather and standalone wind alerts with overlapping validity windows.
rules.mechanism: Winter conditions and strong wind can combine to disrupt travel and power. These alerts may describe the same storm; their probabilities are not independent.
rules.action: Review both alerts before travel and prepare for possible power disruption. This rule does not establish blizzard conditions or road closures.
rules.coverage_note: Checked currently issued alerts for this place; future alerts can still be issued.

rules.title: Inland and coastal flood alerts overlap
rules.threshold: Distinct local inland/flash-flood and coastal-flood/storm-surge alerts with overlapping validity windows.
rules.mechanism: Coastal water levels can impede drainage when inland flooding also occurs. An alert overlap does not establish watershed connectivity, flood depth or inundation at an address.
rules.action: Review both flood messages and local road/emergency guidance. Do not infer a safe route from a gap in mapped alerts.
guidance: NOAA: combined coastal and stormwater flooding
rules.coverage_note: Checked currently issued alerts for this place; future alerts can still be issued.

rules.title: Precipitation chances and stronger winds coincide
rules.threshold: In the same hourly forecast: precipitation chance at least 60% and forecast sustained wind or range maximum at least 25 mph. These are VentusIQ planning thresholds, not NWS warning criteria.
rules.mechanism: The hourly outlook contains both precipitation chances and stronger wind. It does not quantify their joint probability, precipitation intensity or wind gusts.
rules.action: Inspect nearby hours in the activity planner and check official warnings before outdoor activities or driving.
rules.coverage_note: 48.0 of 48 upcoming hours contain the fields needed for this rule. Missing hours are not favorable conditions.

rules.title: Precipitation chances near or below freezing
rules.threshold: In the same hourly forecast: temperature at or below 32Â°F and precipitation chance at least 40%. The probability threshold is a VentusIQ planning choice.
rules.mechanism: Freezing air temperatures and precipitation chances coincide. Air temperature and precipitation probability alone do not establish freezing rain, road temperature or ice accumulation.
rules.action: Review the forecast precipitation type and official winter alerts, and check local road conditions before travel.
guidance: Pennsylvania DMV: cold and wet road conditions
rules.coverage_note: 48.0 of 48 upcoming hours contain the fields needed for this rule. Missing hours are not favorable conditions.

limitations: Rules identify source overlaps and planning thresholds, not joint probabilities, observed impacts, all-clear conditions or a replacement for official instructions.
